summary: The council pattern closes a common governance gap: review output has no value if findings vanish without disposition. It works only when findings are scoped, evidence-linked, and resolved by an accountable authority.

points.text: Each finding needs a stable ID, affected artifact and revision, evidence, severity, concrete risk, proposed check or remedy, owner, and state. Free-form reviewer prose cannot support a reliable loop.
Acceptance must record who accepted which residual risk, why, for how long, and under what compensating control. Marking a thread resolved is not equivalent to a reasoned exception.
A loop budget should cap rounds, elapsed time, and compute, then escalate remaining high-severity disagreements; it must not auto-accept merely because the budget expired.
Council performance should be evaluated by confirmed-finding precision, escaped-defect recall, time to disposition, reopen rate, and reviewer burden, not comment count.
